title: The extension-by-zero exchange morphism
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. All schemes below are separated and of finite type over $k$, and all arrows are $k$-morphisms, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be any commutative condensed ring ([sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]), and let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X' & \xrightarrow{\;g'\;} & X\\
{\scriptstyle j'}\downarrow & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle j}\\
Z' & \xrightarrow{\;g\;} & Z
\end{array}
$$

be a commutative square, so $j\circ g'=g\circ j'$, with $j$ and $j'$ open immersions. Use the restricted pullbacks of [def-sfb-dc-upper-star] and the restricted extensions by zero of [def-sfb-dc-open-lower-shriek]. The *extension-by-zero
exchange morphism* $\mathrm{Ex}^{j}_{sq}\colon j'_!\circ Lg'^*\to Lg^*\circ j_!$ of functors
$D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)\to D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Z',\Lambda)$ is the composite

$$
j'_!Lg'^*\xrightarrow{\ \eta\ }j'_!Lg'^*Lj^*j_!\xrightarrow[\ \sim\ ]{\ \theta\ }j'_!Lj'^*Lg^*j_!\xrightarrow{\ \varepsilon'\ }Lg^*j_!.
$$

Here $\eta$ is the unit of $j_!\dashv Lj^*$ and $\varepsilon'$ the counit of $j'_!\dashv Lj'^*$
([def-sfb-dc-open-lower-shriek-adjunction]). The isomorphism $\theta$ is the pullback
comparison $Lg'^*Lj^*\cong Lj'^*Lg^*$ of [det-def-sfb-base-change-morphism-comparison] for the square
read with $j'$ on top and $g'$, $g$ vertical, whiskered by $j'_!$ on the left and $j_!$ on the right.

Explicitly, if $c_{a,b}\colon L(b\circ a)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}La^*Lb^*$ denotes the composition isomorphism used in that comparison, then
$$
\theta=\bigl(Lg'^*Lj^*\xrightarrow{c_{g',j}^{-1}}L(j\circ g')^*=L(g\circ j')^*\xrightarrow{c_{j',g}}Lj'^*Lg^*\bigr).
$$
For $K\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)$ the component is therefore
$$
\mathrm{Ex}^{j}_{sq,K}
=\varepsilon'_{Lg^*j_!K}\circ j'_!\bigl(\theta_{j_!K}\bigr)\circ j'_!Lg'^*(\eta_K).
$$
This definition uses only commutativity of the square; it does not require the square to be cartesian or any preservation assumption on derived pushforwards.
